problemText: A triangle has a base of 10 meters and a height of 6 meters, measured perpendicular to the base. What is the area of the triangle?
choices: 16 square meters
60 square meters
30 square meters
48 square meters
hints: Recall the triangle area rule: base times height, divided by two.
The height must be perpendicular to the base, not the length of a slanted side.

problemText: A parallelogram has two parallel sides that are each 12 inches long. A side connecting those parallel edges is 8 inches long and slanted. The straight up-and-down distance between the two parallel sides is 5 inches. What is the area of the parallelogram?
choices: 96 square inches
100 square inches
40 square inches
60 square inches
hints: Identify which measurement is perpendicular to the base.
Do not multiply by the length of the slanted side; use only the straight up-and-down distance.

problemText: A rectangle has a length of 9 centimeters and a width of 4 centimeters. One diagonal line is drawn from one corner to the opposite corner, splitting the rectangle into two triangles. What is the area of one of those triangles?
choices: 18 square centimeters
13 square centimeters
36 square centimeters
26 square centimeters
hints: A diagonal splits a rectangle into two matching pieces, each half the rectangle's area.
First find the area of the whole rectangle, then divide by two.

problemText: A composite figure is shaped like a house: a rectangle 8 feet wide and 6 feet tall, with a triangular roof on top. The roof's base is the same as the rectangle's width, and the height of the roof (from base to peak) is 4 feet, measured perpendicular to the base. What is the total area of the entire figure, in square feet?
choices: 80 square feet
112 square feet
64 square feet
48 square feet
hints: Decompose the house into two pieces: a rectangle and a triangle on top.
Find the area of each piece separately, then add them together.

problemText: A trapezoid-shaped garden bed has a bottom edge of 20 meters and a top edge of 12 meters. Both edges run horizontally. The straight up-and-down distance between them is 8 meters. To find the area, Maya cuts the trapezoid into one rectangle and one triangle. If the rectangle uses the shorter top edge as its width, what should be the area of the triangle piece, in square meters?
choices: 64 square meters
96 square meters
32 square meters
48 square meters
hints: The rectangle piece has width 12 meters and height 8 meters; the remaining triangle has its base as what is left of the bottom edge.
The triangle's base is 20 minus 12 equals 8 meters, and its height is the same 8 meters as the rectangle.

problemText: An L-shaped wall panel is made from a large rectangle 16 inches wide and 10 inches tall, with a rectangular notch cut out of the bottom-right corner. The notch is 6 inches wide and 4 inches tall. A student wants to find the area by composing the L-shape into simpler pieces. Which of the following combinations of decomposed pieces would correctly give the area of the L-shaped panel?
choices: A rectangle 16 by 4 (64 square inches) plus a rectangle 10 by 6 (60 square inches), for a total of 124 square inches
A rectangle 10 by 10 (100 square inches) plus a rectangle 6 by 10 (60 square inches), for a total of 160 square inches
A rectangle 16 by 6 (96 square inches) plus a rectangle 10 by 4 (40 square inches), for a total of 136 square inches
A rectangle 16 by 10 (160 square inches) minus a rectangle 6 by 4 (24 square inches), for a total of 136 square inches
hints: You can start with the whole large rectangle and subtract the piece that was removed, or build the L-shape from smaller rectangles by adding them.
Check that the dimensions of each piece match the actual cuts shown; a piece's width and height must match sides that are actually present in the L-shape.

problemText: A polygon has vertices that are plotted on a coordinate plane, then connected in order. After connecting all the vertices to each other in the order given, what must you do to finish drawing the polygon?
choices: Stop after connecting the last two vertices listed
Erase all the plotted points so only the sides remain
Draw a diagonal line from one corner to the opposite corner
Connect the last vertex back to the first vertex to close the shape
hints: Think about what makes a polygon a closed shape with no gaps.
A polygon is closed and flat — how does that happen if you stop at the last vertex?

problemText: A triangular garden has vertices at A(4, 1), B(4, 7), and C(8, 1), where each unit is one meter. What can you say about side AB?
choices: It is vertical because both endpoints have the same first coordinate
It is horizontal because both endpoints have the same first coordinate
It is diagonal because the endpoints do not share a coordinate
It is horizontal because both endpoints have the same second coordinate
hints: Look at what coordinate A and B share: is it the first or second coordinate?
If two points share the same first coordinate, do they run left-right or up-down?

problemText: A rectangular bench has corners at P(2, 5), Q(9, 5), R(9, 8), and S(2, 8), in order. Find the length of side PQ in units.
choices: 3 units
7 units
10 units
5 units
hints: First, check what coordinate P and Q share — that tells you whether the side is horizontal or vertical.
Use only the coordinate that differs between the two points to find the length.

problemText: A parking lot forms a quadrilateral with vertices at M(-3, 4), N(-3, -2), O(5, -2), and P(5, 4), where each unit is one meter. Find the length of side MN and the length of side NO, then add them together.
choices: 10 meters
12 meters
14 meters
16 meters
hints: For side MN, check which coordinate both vertices share. For side NO, do the same — it will be different.
Remember: if the two endpoints are on opposite sides of zero, add the distances from zero instead of subtracting.

problemText: A pentagonal flower bed has vertices at A(1, 6), B(1, -4), C(7, -4), D(7, 2), and E(4, 6), in order. To draw this polygon correctly, you must plot all five vertices and connect them in a specific order, ending by connecting E back to A. Which of these correctly describes side BC and side CD?
choices: Side BC is vertical and 10 units long; side CD is horizontal and 6 units long
Side BC is vertical and 11 units long; side CD is horizontal and 5 units long
Side BC is horizontal and 6 units long; side CD is vertical and 6 units long
Side BC is horizontal and 6 units long; side CD is vertical and 10 units long
hints: For side BC: B and C share one coordinate — identify which one. For side CD: C and D share a different coordinate.
When finding lengths, remember to check whether both points are on the same side of zero or opposite sides.

problemText: A hexagonal walking path has vertices at U(-5, 3), V(-5, -4), W(2, -4), X(2, 1), Y(6, 1), and Z(6, 3), listed in order. To close the shape, you will draw a final segment from Z back to U. Which of these statements is true about the side lengths of this polygon?
choices: Sides UV and WX are both vertical, and side UV is 7 units while side WX is 5 units
Sides UV and WX are both horizontal, and they are equal in length
Side ZU is diagonal, and sides UV and WX are both vertical with the same length
Sides VW and XY are both horizontal and equal to each other, and side UV is vertical and 6 units long
hints: Sketch or list each consecutive pair of vertices. Identify which sides are vertical by looking at which coordinates match.
For each vertical side, remember the rule: if endpoints are on opposite sides of zero, add their distances from zero.

problemText: A rectangular prism has edge lengths of 2 inches, 3 inches, and 4 inches. What does the volume of this prism represent?
choices: The number of unit cubes with edge length 1 inch needed to pack the prism completely with no gaps or leftover cubes
The total distance around all edges of the prism when measured and added together as a sum of lengths
The total area covered by multiplying the length and width of the base rectangular face
The distance you travel if you walk around the perimeter of the prism's bottom face one complete time
hints: Think about what 'packing' the prism means — what are you actually counting?
Volume uses cubes, not flat shapes. Which choice talks about cubes?

problemText: A rectangular prism measures 2 inches long, 3 inches wide, and 1 inch tall. Using the formula V = l × w × h, what is its volume?
choices: 6 square inches
6 cubic inches
5 cubic inches
12 cubic inches
hints: Multiply the three edge lengths together: 2 × 3 × 1.
Volume is always measured in cubic units, not square units. Which choice uses the correct unit?

problemText: You want to pack a small rectangular prism with side lengths of 1/2 inch, 1/2 inch, and 1 inch using small unit fraction cubes. What edge length should each small cube have so that it fits a whole number of times along every edge of the prism?
choices: 1/4 inch
1 inch
1/2 inch
2 inches
hints: Find a unit fraction that divides evenly into 1/2 inch and also into 1 inch.
A smaller cube fits better. Check: does 1/2 divide evenly into 1/2, and into 1?

problemText: A rectangular jewelry box measures 3/4 inch long, 1/2 inch wide, and 1/2 inch tall. To find its volume using the packing method, you choose small cubes with edge length 1/4 inch. How many small cubes will fit in the box, and what is the volume of one small cube?
choices: 12 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/8 cubic inch
6 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/8 cubic inch
24 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/64 cubic inch
12 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/64 cubic inch
hints: Count how many 1/4-inch cubes fit along each edge: divide 3/4 ÷ 1/4, then 1/2 ÷ 1/4, then 1/2 ÷ 1/4, and multiply those counts.
A cube with edge 1/4 inch has volume 1/4 × 1/4 × 1/4. Work out this multiplication carefully.

problemText: Two rectangular prisms are packed with unit cubes. Prism A measures 2 inches by 2 inches by 2 inches. Prism B measures 1/2 inch by 1/2 inch by 1/2 inch. Which statement correctly compares their volumes?
choices: Prism A has a volume of 8 cubic inches and Prism B has a volume of 1/8 cubic inch, so Prism A holds 64 times as many unit cubes
Prism A has a volume of 4 cubic inches and Prism B has a volume of 1/4 cubic inch, so Prism A holds 16 times as many unit cubes
Both prisms hold the same volume because they are both cubes
Prism A holds 8 unit cubes and Prism B holds 1/2 unit cube, so they cannot be compared
hints: Calculate V = l × w × h for each prism separately. Remember that fractional edges give fractional volumes.
To compare volumes, divide the larger by the smaller: 8 ÷ (1/8) = ?

problemText: A rectangular prism measures 5/4 inches long, 2/3 inch wide, and 3/2 inches tall. You want to pack it with small cubes. What is the smallest edge length a unit fraction cube can have so that it fits a whole number of times along every edge? Then calculate the volume of the prism using the formula V = l × w × h. Show that your chosen cube size works.
choices: 1/6 inch; the volume is 5/8 cubic inches; and 1/6 fits evenly into all three edges when written with denominator 6 because 5/4 = 7.5/6, 2/3 = 4/6, and 3/2 = 9/6
1/12 inch; the volume is 5/16 cubic inches; and 1/12 divides evenly into all three edges because they share a common denominator of 12
1/4 inch; the volume is 15/8 cubic inches; and 1/4 is smaller than all three edge lengths so it will divide into each one
1/2 inch; the volume is 5/4 cubic inches; and 1/2 divides all whole numbers because it is a unit fraction with a small denominator
hints: Rewrite each edge with a common denominator. What is the least common denominator of 4, 3, and 2? Once you find it, the unit fraction cube should have edge length equal to the denominator of that common form, written as a unit fraction.

After choosing your cube size, multiply the three edge lengths using the formula. Check that your cube choice divides evenly: 5/4 ÷ 1/12 = ?, 2/3 ÷ 1/12 = ?, 3/2 ÷ 1/12 = ? (all should be whole numbers).

problemText: A net is a flat pattern of two-dimensional shapes that folds up to form a three-dimensional solid. What does the term 'surface area' mean in relation to a net?
choices: The area of only the largest face in the net, measured by finding which individual rectangle or polygon has the greatest area and using only that measurement
The total area of every face on the outside of the solid, found by adding up the area of each flat piece in the net
The perimeter of the net when all of its pieces are arranged in a line, calculated by measuring around the outer edge of the entire flat pattern
The area of the space inside the solid after it has been folded up from the net, which represents the volume rather than the outer covering
hints: Think about what 'surface' means — it refers to the outside covering of an object, not the inside.
Surface area is found by calculating the area of each individual flat piece and combining them together.

problemText: A rectangular prism-shaped storage container has a net with six rectangles. Three of those rectangles have dimensions 5 cm × 8 cm, and the other three rectangles have different dimensions. Why must the other three rectangles have the same dimensions as each other, even though they are different from the first three?
choices: Because the three larger rectangles need three smaller rectangles to balance the net and keep all edges aligned properly when folded
Because all rectangles in a net must follow a pattern where every other rectangle is the same size to ensure the net folds without gaps or overlaps
Because a rectangular prism has six faces that form three matching pairs, and faces in each pair must have identical dimensions
Because the net's arrangement requires matching dimensions for rectangles that will eventually touch each other at shared edges when the solid is formed
hints: Recall the structure of a rectangular prism: opposite faces match each other.
In a net, each pair of opposite faces (top-bottom, front-back, left-right) must be identical in size.

problemText: A triangular prism's net contains two triangles and three rectangles. The triangle has sides of lengths 5 m, 5 m, and 6 m. When the net is folded into a solid, what are the widths of the three rectangles in the net?
choices: The widths cannot be determined from the information given in the problem
5 m, 6 m, and 6 m, because the two matching sides wrap identical rectangles
All three rectangles are 5 m wide, because that is the most common side length
5 m, 5 m, and 6 m, because each rectangle wraps around one side of the triangle
hints: Remember that each rectangular face connects along one side of the triangle once folded.
The width of each rectangle must match the length of the side of the triangle it wraps around.

problemText: A rectangular prism has dimensions 7 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 3 inches tall. A student starts to find its surface area by drawing a net with six rectangles. They correctly calculate the areas of four rectangles as 7 × 3 = 21, 7 × 3 = 21, 7 × 5 = 35, and 7 × 5 = 35 square inches. What is the total surface area, and what are the areas of the two remaining rectangles?
choices: The two remaining rectangles are each 5 × 3 = 15 square inches; total surface area is 142 square inches
The two remaining rectangles are each 7 × 5 = 35 square inches; total surface area is 182 square inches
The two remaining rectangles are each 5 × 5 = 25 square inches; total surface area is 156 square inches
The remaining rectangles cannot have equal areas, so the prism cannot have a valid net
hints: A rectangular prism has three matching pairs of opposite faces. The student has found two pairs already; think about what dimensions the remaining pair must have.
The third pair of faces represents the two ends of the prism — their dimensions should be width × height.

problemText: A student draws a net for a rectangular prism with dimensions 8 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm and labels the edges where rectangles meet. Two rectangles in the net are supposed to attach along an edge labeled 8 cm on one rectangle and 6 cm on the other. The student wants to know if this net will fold correctly. Explain why or why not, then determine the correct surface area.
choices: The net will fold correctly because 8 and 6 are close enough in length to attach; the correct surface area is 208 square centimeters
The net will not fold correctly because shared edges must have matching lengths; the correct surface area is 208 square centimeters
The net will not fold correctly because the prism's dimensions are not in the right order; the correct surface area is 192 square centimeters
The net will fold correctly, and any two edge lengths can be matched in a valid net; the correct surface area is 200 square centimeters
hints: Check the rule about shared edges: two faces that touch once folded must share an edge of exactly the same length in the net.
Calculate the surface area by finding the areas of the three pairs: 8×6, 8×4, and 6×4, then doubling the sum.

problemText: A triangular prism pencil holder has two identical triangular ends. Each triangle has a base of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. The pencil holder is 12 cm long between the two triangular ends. A student calculates the area of the two triangles as 6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 square centimeters for both combined. They then add areas of two rectangles that wrap around the triangle's base and height, getting 6 × 12 = 72 and 4 × 12 = 48 square centimeters. Their total is 12 + 72 + 48 = 132 square centimeters. Identify the error and find the correct surface area.
choices: The student double-counted the triangular ends by including both triangles when only one should be measured for the net; the correct surface area is 120 square centimeters
The student incorrectly calculated the triangle area using the formula for a parallelogram instead of a triangle; the correct surface area is 144 square centimeters
The student forgot to include the hypotenuse of the triangle as a third rectangular face; the correct surface area is 162 square centimeters
The student miscalculated the dimensions of the rectangles by using individual triangle dimensions instead of the prism's actual edge lengths; the correct surface area is 156 square centimeters
hints: Recall that a triangular prism has five faces total: two triangles and three rectangles. Count how many rectangles the student included.
The hypotenuse (the slanted side of the right triangle) is also a side of the triangle that must wrap around with its own rectangular face.
